PLO1.title: Socio-Ecological Sustainability
PLO1.description: Apply socio-ecologically sustainable processes and research to design transformative communication strategies that promote a diverse, equitable, and just society.
PLO1.assessment_question: To what extent does the thesis demonstrate socio-ecological awareness and apply research or design processes that engage questions of sustainability, equity, interdependence, or transformation?

manifestations.description: The thesis situates its inquiry within relevant historical, social, political, economic, or cultural conditions. Evidence may include discussion of broader structures, histories, inequalities, institutions, or conditions that shape the subject of the thesis.

The work acknowledges the designer or researcher’s position in relation to the subject and considers ethical questions that may affect the research or design process. Evidence may include attention to positionality, bias, consent, representation, responsibility, or the consequences of design decisions.

The work documents engagement with relevant people, communities, participants, or stakeholders as part of the research or design process. Evidence may include interviews, observations, workshops, participatory activities, consultation, critique, or other forms of field engagement.

The work considers environmental conditions or the relationship between human activity and ecological systems. Evidence may include attention to materials, resources, environmental impact, living systems, or the interdependence of social and ecological conditions.

PLO2.title: Situated Knowledge
PLO2.description: Integrate situated knowledge and perspectives with the histories, principles, and practices of communications design to create speculative artifacts, modes of representation, platforms, or systems that serve intersectional identities and abilities.
PLO2.assessment_question: To what extent is the student's understanding and design response shaped by knowledge grounded in particular people, places, histories, bodies, identities, experiences, or conditions?

manifestations.description: The work foregrounds knowledge grounded in particular communities, cultures, places, identities, or lived experiences. Evidence may include personal narratives, local or marginalized perspectives, challenges to dominant or universalizing narratives, or acts of self-historicization in which students locate themselves as subjects of and within their own work.

The work draws on forms of knowing that emerge through experience, participation, sensory engagement, embodiment, or making. Evidence may include tacit knowledge, material exploration, bodily experience, observation, participation, or other forms of knowledge that go beyond abstract or textual research.

The work situates the inquiry in relation to past, present, or future conditions. Evidence may include historical context, comparison with relevant designers, movements, practices, or theories, as well as speculative or future-oriented propositions.

The work brings together research, experience, context, and design practice to construct an interpretation, argument, or position. Evidence may include synthesis and reflection, connections across different forms of knowledge, and the development of a coherent relationship between the thesis inquiry and its design manifestations.

PLO3.title: Critical Discourse
PLO3.description: Engage interdisciplinary knowledge and critical discourse in developing a significant body of work characterized by experimentation, creativity, resilience, and inclusion of non-dominant ways of knowing, thinking, and doing.
PLO3.assessment_question: To what extent does the thesis construct and develop a critical position through engagement with multiple forms of knowledge, discourse, experimentation, and design practice?

manifestations.description: The work establishes a discernible position or standpoint in relation to the thesis topic. Evidence may include an explicit statement of position, an argument, critique, proposition, or other indication of how the student positions themselves in relation to the subject.

The work develops a position, voice, language, or mode of expression through the progression of the thesis. Evidence may include shifts in framing, iterative development, the emergence of a visual or conceptual language, or increasingly specific ways of articulating the thesis position.

The work brings together ideas, methods, theories, or practices from different disciplines as part of the inquiry. Evidence may include combinations of methods or forms of knowledge that inform how the project is framed, investigated, or developed.

The work interprets or translates ideas, knowledge, information, or relationships into visual, symbolic, material, spatial, narrative, or other forms of representation. Evidence may include visualization, mapping, symbolic systems, visual metaphors, or other designed forms used to make complex ideas perceptible or communicable.

The thesis includes multiple related artifacts, experiments, studies, iterations, propositions, or manifestations that collectively constitute a sustained body of inquiry. Evidence may appear through the accumulation and development of work across the thesis rather than through a single final outcome.

PLO4.title: Numerous Technologies
PLO4.description: Exhibit versatility with tools and strategies across multiple technologies that recognize design as a collective action addressing socio-economic and environmental issues.
PLO4.assessment_question: To what extent does the thesis demonstrate purposeful versatility across tools, technologies, media, materials, or modes of production?

manifestations.manifestation: Diverse Modes of Learning and Thinking
manifestations.description: The work engages different ways of learning, thinking, or experiencing. Evidence may include visual, auditory, tactile, kinesthetic, spatial, embodied, interactive, or other modes that contribute to the development or communication of the thesis.

The work uses or combines multiple media, tools, technologies, or material processes. Evidence may include combinations of video, audio, text, physical artifacts, digital systems, analog processes, varied materials, fabrication methods, or movement between analog and digital tools.

The work demonstrates development through repeated testing, variation, and revision. Evidence may include prototypes, drafts, multiple options, scenarios, tests, failed attempts, multiphase processes, changes in direction, or successive versions of the work.

The work translates ideas, information, experiences, or content from one medium, format, or system into another. Evidence may include movement from data to visualization, text to image, physical experience to digital form, sound to visual form, research to artifact, or one representational system to another.
